content.title: What is a Substring?
content.description: A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters extracted from a string. The characters must appear in the same order and occupy consecutive positions.

content.content: Substring problems are among the most frequently asked topics in coding interviews. Many string-based questions involve finding, counting, comparing, or optimizing substrings based on specific conditions.

content.title: Important Note
content.content: A substring is always contiguous, whereas a subsequence can skip characters.
Understanding Substrings
Every string contains multiple possible substrings. By selecting different starting and ending positions, we can generate numerous valid substrings.

content.title: Formula
content.description: For a string of length n, the total number of substrings is n × (n + 1) / 2.

content.content: Common Types of Substring Problems

items.question: Longest Unique Substring
items.answer: Find the longest substring without repeating characters.

items.question: Substring Search
items.answer: Determine whether a pattern exists within a string.

items.question: Longest Palindromic Substring
items.answer: Find the longest substring that reads the same forward and backward.

items.question: Minimum Window Substring
items.answer: Find the smallest substring containing all required characters.

content.content: Longest Unique Substring
One of the most popular interview problems asks us to find the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.
Substring Search
Substring search determines whether a smaller pattern exists inside a larger string. Search engines, editors, and text-processing systems use this operation extensively.

content.title: Real-World Usage
content.content: Search bars, browser find features, and autocomplete systems perform substring searches continuously.
Longest Palindromic Substring
A palindrome is a string that reads the same forward and backward. This problem asks us to find the longest palindromic substring within a given string.

content.title: Key Observation
content.description: Every palindrome expands around a center. This observation helps optimize the solution.

content.content: Minimum Window Substring
This advanced Sliding Window problem requires finding the smallest substring that contains all characters of another string.
Sliding Window & Substrings
Most optimized substring problems use the Sliding Window technique because substrings are always contiguous.

content.title: Interview Pattern
content.content: Whenever a problem mentions longest substring, shortest substring, unique characters, or window size, think about Sliding Window.
Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Reading a Sentence
content.content: Imagine highlighting consecutive words in a sentence. The highlighted section forms a substring. Expanding or shrinking the highlighted area is similar to the Sliding Window technique.
Common Mistakes

items.question: What is the most common mistake?
Why do solutions become slow?
items.answer: Generating and checking every possible substring repeatedly.

items.question: Why is Sliding Window preferred?
items.answer: It avoids redundant computations and processes characters efficiently.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Most substring interview questions can be solved using Sliding Window, Hash Maps, Character Frequency Arrays, or Two Pointer techniques.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Substrings are contiguous portions of a string.
Sliding Window is the most important substring technique.
Longest Unique Substring is a classic interview problem.
Minimum Window Substring is a popular advanced question.
Substring problems frequently use Hash Maps and Two Pointers.
